title: Edge-side OTLP Buffer and Backpressure Filter for Inference KPI Integrity
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Scope: Implement an edge-side OTLP buffering and backpressure filter that sits in front of the existing OTLP/Prometheus ingestion pipeline for inference requests. The goal is to make metric delivery resilient during transient network congestion and spike traffic without altering per-request attribution or cardinality profiles. This ticket covers design, a lightweight golang sidecar implementation, e2e tests, and a canary rollout plan for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Problem: We see dropped or delayed inference KPIs during regional network spikes and noisy tenants, causing SLO violations and inaccurate latency/error dashboards. Existing ingest proxies accept bursts but lack tenant-aware backpressure and local buffering that guarantees eventual delivery while avoiding high-memory OOMs on nodes.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Buffer OTLP metric points on the edge for up to 30s under transient connectivity loss without data loss for critical KPI labels (model, tenant, route).
- Implement a backpressure filter that downsamples non-critical metrics under sustained overload using tenant-aware sampling policies.
- Preserve accuracy for SLI/KPI enumerations used by Console dashboards (latency P50/P95/P99, errors per 1k requests, kv-cache hit ratio).
- Emit observability for the sidecar itself: buffer depth, dropped points, sampling rate per-tenant, oldest-point-age.
- No increase in tail latency for inference responses; sidecar must be asynchronous to RPC path.
- Automated integration tests simulating 3 failure modes: network partition to telemetry backend, tenant traffic spike, schema/label explosion.

Design summary:
- Sidecar process (go) with small embedded LRU for recent series to group points; ring-buffer segmented by tenant and priority class.
- Two delivery strategies: fast-forward (push immediately when backend healthy) and graceful-drain (rate-limited flush under recovery).
- Backpressure policy DSL: per-tenant budget + global budget + penalty for high-cardinality label sets. Policy pulled from platform configs (overrides for enterprise customers).
- Lightweight in-memory retention (configurable, default 30s) + bounded disk spillover for Dedicated nodes with limited disk quota.
- Expose Prometheus metrics and OTLP traces for the sidecar; integrate traces with existing request-level tracing hooks to correlate dropped points with request spans.

Rollout plan:
- Feature branch + unit tests -> staged integration in telemetry-ci harness -> canary on a small set of Dedicated nodes (low-traffic tenants) -> broaden to Dedicated fleet -> opt-in private deployment preview -> enable by default after 4-week monitoring window.

Risks and mitigations:
- Memory blowup under cardinality explosion: mitigate by strict per-tenant series caps and earliest-drop policy with metric sampling.
- Double-counting during retries: attach idempotency keys and dedupe at ingestion gateway (follow-up ticket if needed).
- Sensitive telemetry writes to disk: encrypt spillover files and require KMS key for Private deployments.

Out-of-scope:
- Long-term archival of buffered telemetry beyond 24 hours.
